competitors.title: Building a serverless A2A gateway for agent discovery, routing, and access control (AWS Blog, Jul 2026)
key_points: AWS published a reference implementation for a serverless A2A gateway with three layers: Management (centralized agent registry with discovery and semantic search), Control (fine-grained access control using JWT scopes and Lambda authorizer), and Execution (single-domain routing with OAuth backend authentication and SSE streaming)
Gateway uses Amazon API Gateway REST API as single entry point, Lambda authorizer for JWT scope validation, DynamoDB for agent registry and permissions, and Secrets Manager for backend credentials
Agent Registry maps agent IDs to backend URLs, auth configs, and cached agent cards; Permissions table maps JWT scopes to allowed agents
Semantic agent discovery using Amazon Titan Text Embeddings in Bedrock, stored in Amazon S3 Vectors
Supports both A2A protocol bindings: JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON/REST, with endpoints like GET /agents/{agentId}/.well-known/agent-card.json and POST /agents/{agentId}
Management endpoints: GET /agents (list), POST /search (semantic search), POST /admin/agents/register, POST /admin/agents/{agentId}/sync, POST /admin/agents/{agentId}/status
Rate limiting via DynamoDB atomic counters with TTL-based auto-expiry; per-user, per-agent rate limits at proxy layer
Optional VPC private deployment mode with private API Gateway endpoint; supports AWS Cloud WAN for on-premises/other-cloud agents
Terraform-provisioned; includes deployable example agents (Weather Agent, Calculator Agent)

angles: AWS's approach to MCP governance: Bedrock AgentCore handles MCP server integration as action groups, while the A2A gateway provides centralized agent registry, discovery, routing, and access control — together forming a complete governance stack

The three-layer governance model: Management (agent registry + semantic search), Control (JWT scope-based access control), Execution (single-domain routing with OAuth backend auth) — how AWS implements this with serverless services
AWS vs Microsoft vs open-source: AWS uses A2A protocol + Bedrock AgentCore, Microsoft uses Agent 365 + Entra ID, open-source uses Bifrost/Obot — comparing governance approaches for MCP at scale
The MCP Server Cards standard: how .well-known URLs enable automated discovery and registry population, and how AWS's agent card caching fits this pattern
Skills over MCP: bundling domain-specific instructions with tools — how this enables governed skill distribution across enterprise agent fleets
From point-to-point to gateway: the N×M integration problem and why AWS's A2A gateway pattern is the production answer for enterprises with 20+ agents
Security at scale: OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow, JWT scope enforcement, Lambda authorizer, Secrets Manager for backend credentials — AWS's security model for agent-to-agent communication
